content.text: The text first describes Congreve rockets: their construction, ranges, durability, ammunition varieties, parachute flares, and claimed economy versus conventional artillery. It then follows Civil War St. Louis through Camp Jackson, shifting loyalties, martial law, refugee suffering, auctions, and divided families. Stephen Brice serves the Union, saves John Brinsmade, rises under General Sherman, and repeatedly encounters Clarence Colfax. Virginia Carvel nurses wounded soldiers, cares for Judge Whipple, rejects Eliphalet Hopper’s coercive proposal, and reunites with her father. Judge Whipple dies in his office while Virginia plays “Lead, Kindly Light.” Stephen confronts Hopper there. Later, Stephen serves with Sherman in western campaigns and the March to the Sea. In 1865, at Goldsboro, he recognizes Clarence, captured in civilian clothes while carrying Confederate messages, and asks Sherman to spare him.
